sections.label: THINKING
sections.content:
Clicking on the empty gray cell (40,25) also only changed the timer (this time two cells: (0,61) and (0,62) P→c). Interesting — the first click consumed 1 cell, and the second consumed 2 cells? Maybe the timer shrinks by an increasing amount, or it's time-based (elapsed real time). run_elapsed_seconds was about 150, time_remaining was 7770. The timer might be based on real time, not on the number of actions. In fact, the first probe: 1 cell changed. The second: 2 cells changed. The time between actions was different. So the pink strip is a real-time countdown bar, decreasing at a constant rate (cells per second). This is a HUD timer, not a puzzle element.
So both clicks had no effect on the board. Clicking on the piece's center and clicking on an empty cell did nothing. So what does a click do? Maybe a click only has an effect when clicking on a specific object: the yellow gap in the bar, the blue square, the yellow strip. Or maybe a click "places" something only under specific conditions.
Let me try clicking the yellow gap in the black bar: (29, 38).

sections.label: ASSISTANT
sections.content:
World model (revised): Both probe clicks (on the piece, on empty gray) changed only the pink top strip (timer shrinking by real time, 1–2 cells per action) — no board effect. So generic clicks are inert; the puzzle must react to specific objects. Candidates: yellow gap in black bar (rows 28–31, cols 38–39), blue squares (cols 60–63), yellow strip (cols 50–51, rows 44–49).
Plan: click the yellow gap in the bar at (29,38) and diff.
